summary: Composio already provides a managed Google OAuth app for Google Calendar, so you can connect users today with no registration. If you want your own branding, scopes or quota, create a Google Cloud OAuth client. A public custom app that uses the Calendar scopes Composio defaults to (calendar, calendar.events) must pass Google's OAuth verification, which developers report is slow in 2026. Biggest gotcha: while a custom app's consent screen is in Testing status, refresh tokens expire after 7 days.

verdict.difficultyReason: Self-serve and instant via Composio's managed app, but a custom app for arbitrary users needs Google sensitive-scope verification, reported to take weeks to months.

devReady.estimate: 0 min with the Composio managed app; 30-60 min with your own Google Cloud OAuth client
devReady.detail: Managed app: create a Composio connection and sign in (consent screen says Composio). Own app: create the client with the consent screen in Testing and add test users. Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days and only listed test users can connect.

productionReady.estimate: Immediate with the Composio managed app (shared quota); custom app: Google's panel reportedly says 4-6 weeks, developers report 2-3+ months in 2026
productionReady.detail: Publish the custom app to In production and submit for verification: scope justification, demo video, privacy policy, homepage, authorized domain. Until verified, users see an unverified-app warning. A user cap of 100 for unverified apps is commonly cited but I did not confirm it on an official page. Narrower scopes (e.g. calendar.events.owned, calendar.app.created) may reduce friction, but their sensitivity level was not confirmed.

verdict.handsOnEffort: 0 hours (managed) or 3-6 hours for own app plus verification materials

nextAction: Create a Composio connection for googlecalendar using the managed app at https://dashboard.composio.dev and test with your own Google account. Start a custom app only if you need your own branding, scopes or quota.

accessPaths.name: Composio managed app
accessPaths.whenToUse: Prototypes, internal tools, anything where a 'Composio' consent screen is acceptable.
accessPaths.limits: Default scopes only (calendar, calendar.events), quota shared across Composio users, 15-minute minimum trigger polling.

accessPaths.name: Own app, Testing status
accessPaths.whenToUse: Developing and testing your own client with up to a handful of named test users.
accessPaths.limits: Only listed test users; refresh tokens expire after 7 days (documented by Google).

accessPaths.name: Own app, In production but unverified
accessPaths.whenToUse: Small pilots where users can click through a warning.
accessPaths.limits: Unverified-app warning screen; user cap reported (commonly 100) but not confirmed by me.

accessPaths.name: Own app, verified
accessPaths.whenToUse: Public product with your own branding and no warning screen.
accessPaths.timeline: Reported 4-6 weeks target; 2-3+ months reported in 2026 forum threads
accessPaths.limits: Annual re-verification applies to restricted scopes; Calendar scopes are not expected to be restricted (unconfirmed).

prerequisites.detail: Needed only for a custom app. Create at console.cloud.google.com and enable the Google Calendar API.
Dashboard at dashboard.composio.dev for managed or custom auth configs.
Public URLs on a domain you own; required on the consent screen for verification.
Verify in Google Search Console and add it under Authorized domains.
YouTube video showing the OAuth flow, the consent screen with client ID, and where each scope is used.
Written explanation per sensitive scope; draft below.

phases.title: Option A: use Composio managed app
phases.goal: A user can connect Google Calendar with no Google setup.

steps.title: Create a connection with default auth
steps.detail: Use toolkit slug googlecalendar without specifying authConfigs. Sign in with your Google account and approve the Composio consent screen.

phases.title: Register your own Google OAuth app
phases.goal: Working OAuth flow through your own client in Testing mode.

steps.title: Create project and enable API
steps.detail: In Google Cloud Console create a project, then APIs & Services > Library > Google Calendar API > Enable.

steps.title: Configure consent screen
steps.detail: Google Auth Platform / OAuth consent screen: set app name, support email, User type External, add privacy policy and homepage links and authorized domain. Leave in Testing and add your Google accounts as test users.

steps.title: Add scopes
steps.detail: Add https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events (Composio defaults), or narrower scopes if your use case allows.

steps.title: Create OAuth client
steps.detail: Credentials > Create credentials > OAuth client ID > Web application. Add authorized redirect URI exactly: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Copy Client ID and Secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Dashboard > Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Google Calendar > OAuth2 > paste Client ID/Secret > Create. Copy the ac_... ID and pass it in the session authConfigs keyed by googlecalendar.

steps.title: Test connection
steps.detail: Connect with a test user. Expect refresh tokens to die after 7 days while in Testing.

phases.title: Go live with your own app
phases.goal: Any Google user can connect without a warning screen.
phases.waitTime: Reported 4-6 weeks target; 2-3+ months reported by some developers in 2026

steps.title: Publish to production
steps.detail: On the consent screen page click Publish app. Apps in Testing cannot be submitted for verification.

steps.title: Prepare materials
steps.detail: Scope justification, demo video, working privacy policy on your verified domain. Use the drafts below.

steps.title: Submit for verification and respond to Trust & Safety
steps.detail: Submit in the Verification Center. Reviewers email project owners/editors; keep those contacts monitored and reply in the thread.

steps.title: Fallback while waiting
steps.detail: Use the Composio managed app for users, or keep users on the unverified warning flow for pilots.

scopes.purpose: Full read/write on all calendars, including deletion.
scopes.reviewNote: Triggers verification for public apps (Google says sensitive/restricted scopes need verification; the classification of this specific scope is from my knowledge, not a page I fetched). Justify why narrower scopes won't do.

scopes.purpose: Read and edit events on all calendars.
scopes.reviewNote: Triggers verification; developers report a 5+ week review for this scope.
Still likely sensitive; classification not confirmed.

scopes.purpose: Manage events only on calendars the user owns.
scopes.reviewNote: Narrower option; sensitivity level not confirmed.

scopes.purpose: Create secondary calendars and manage events only on them.
scopes.reviewNote: Likely non-sensitive, but unconfirmed. Check the scope label in the Console.

blockers.title: Verification stuck in review
blockers.symptom: Verification Center shows 'under review' for weeks with no Trust & Safety email, often at the privacy policy step.
blockers.fix: Make sure the privacy policy is public, on your verified domain, and names Google user data usage. Reply in the existing email thread if one exists; otherwise post in Google's developer community. Use the Composio managed app meanwhile.

blockers.title: Refresh token expires after 7 days
blockers.symptom: Users must re-authenticate weekly; invalid_grant on refresh.
blockers.fix: Publish the app to In production. Does not apply to the Composio managed app.

blockers.title: Oldest refresh token silently invalidated
blockers.symptom: Connections break when one account authorizes the same client more than 100 times.
blockers.fix: Reuse existing connections; avoid repeated re-auth for the same user and client.

blockers.title: Unregistered or wrong client
blockers.symptom: invalid_client / 'The OAuth client was not found' on the authorize page.
blockers.fix: Check the client ID in the Composio auth config and that the redirect URI exactly matches.

blockers.title: Unused tokens expire
blockers.symptom: Refresh token dead after 6 months of no use.
blockers.fix: Prompt re-connection or use the connection periodically.

technical.pkce: Supported (S256 and plain) per discovery metadata; optional for web server clients with a secret.
technical.refreshTokens: Pass access_type=offline (and typically prompt=consent) to get a refresh token. Expires after 7 days in Testing status for external apps, after 6 months of non-use, and the 100-per-account-per-client limit silently invalidates the oldest. Access tokens are short-lived (typically 1 hour; not verified on a fetched page).
technical.redirectUriRules: Exact match against URIs registered on the OAuth client. Register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. HTTPS is required for non-localhost URIs (from my knowledge; not re-verified).
technical.notes: Console is behind Google sign-in (probe redirected to login). Composio managed app has shared quota and 15-minute minimum trigger polling. Google Workspace admins can block third-party apps for their domain, so enterprise users may need admin approval.

drafts.title: Scope justification
drafts.purpose: Google Verification Center scope justification field
drafts.content: [APP NAME] is an AI assistant that lets users manage their Google Calendar by chat. We request https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events so the assistant can read the user's events to answer schedule questions and create, update and delete events the user explicitly asks for. We request [calendar / calendar.readonly only if needed] to [list calendars / reason]. Calendar data is only used to perform user-requested actions, is not sold, is not used for advertising or to train generalized AI models, and is stored [encrypted / not stored]. Narrower scopes such as calendar.app.created do not work because [REASON]. Privacy policy: [URL].

drafts.title: Demo video outline
drafts.purpose: Script for the required YouTube demo video
drafts.content:
1. Show app homepage and domain [DOMAIN].
2. Click Connect Google Calendar.
3. Show the Google consent screen with the browser URL and client_id visible, and the requested scopes.
4. Approve and return to the app.
5. Show a feature using each scope (e.g. 'what's on my calendar tomorrow' for events read; 'schedule lunch Friday' for event create).
6. Show how users disconnect/delete data.

drafts.title: Reviewer note
drafts.content: Hello, our app [APP NAME] (project ID [PROJECT_ID]) uses Calendar scopes only for user-initiated actions. Privacy policy at [URL] covers Google user data under 'Google API Services User Data Policy' including Limited Use. Test account for reviewers: [EMAIL / instructions]. Please let us know what else you need.

probes.observed: Found OIDC metadata: authorize https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, PKCE plain and S256, grants include authorization_code and refresh_token.

probes.action: Authorize probe with unregistered client_id and Composio redirect URI
probes.observed: 302 to signin/oauth/error with authError decoding to invalid_client ('The OAuth client was not found'); no redirect back to Composio.
probes.conclusion: Endpoint live; unregistered clients get an invalid_client error page.

uncertainties: Official sensitivity labels for each Calendar scope were not visible in the fetched pages; calendar and calendar.events being sensitive comes from my background knowledge. Check the scope labels in the Console.
The 100-user cap for unverified apps was not confirmed on a fetched official page.
The 4-6 week and 3-5 day figures come from forum posts quoting the Verification Center, not an official page I read.
Whether new narrow scopes (calendar.events.owned, calendar.app.created, freebusy) are non-sensitive is unconfirmed.
Google Workspace admin restrictions and any 2026 policy changes beyond forum reports were not researched in depth.
Only a real logged-in setup would confirm current Console menu names (Google Auth Platform layout).
